domain.label: the charge-stage chain (electrical)
domain.mapping: Six charge-storage stages in a chain (stage 1 at the source end, stage 6 at the load end). Quantity: units of stored charge. Capacity: a stage's rated charge. Spill-over: a breakdown shunt that passes excess charge to the next stage down the chain, handled stage by stage from 1 to 6; excess from stage 6 goes to ground. The two states: a comparator with hysteresis (a Schmitt trigger) that is ASSERTED or CLEAR; it asserts at the upper threshold and clears only at the lower one. Release step: a clear stage leaks a quarter of its charge to ground; an asserted stage feeds back half of its charge to the previous stage through a return diode, computed from all stages' readings before any is changed. Global reset: a breaker trip that halves every stage, the removed charge going to ground. Loss tally: total charge sent to ground.

translation.document:
Six stages in a chain: 1 at the source, 6 at the load. Every cycle runs five moves in order, each finished chain-wide before the next. Everything starts CLEAR; ground tally starts at zero.

Ratings, stages 1 to 6: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7. Upper thresholds: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5. Lower thresholds: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2. Starting charge: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1. Breaker setting: 38 total.

1. Charge in. Add the cycle's feed to each stage; ratings aren't enforced here.
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

2. Shunts. Walk 1 to 6. A stage over rating dumps the excess into the next stage down and sits at exactly rating; stage 6's excess goes to ground. Walking in order, 1's excess can tip 2 before you reach 2.

3. Comparators. Read each stage now. CLEAR goes ASSERTED at or above its upper threshold; ASSERTED goes CLEAR at or below its lower. In between it holds. Log every flip.

4. Bleed. Take all six readings first, then move everything at once. A CLEAR stage leaks a quarter, rounded down, to ground. An ASSERTED stage sends half, rounded down, back through its return diode to the stage before; stage 1's goes to ground. Ratings aren't checked here, so a stage can sit over until next cycle's shunts, or for good after cycle 5.

5. Breaker. Sum the chain. Strictly over 38, every stage halves, rounded down, the difference to ground; note the cycle. At 38 or under, nothing.

Report. End of cycle 5, charge 1 to 6: 6, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2. States: ASSERTED, ASSERTED, ASSERTED, ASSERTED, ASSERTED, CLEAR. Flips (cycle, position, before, after): (1,2,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (1,3,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (1,4,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (1,5,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (2,1,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (2,3,ASSERTED,CLEAR) (2,5,ASSERTED,CLEAR) (2,6,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (3,3,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (3,4,ASSERTED,CLEAR) (4,4,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (4,5,CLEAR,ASSERTED) (5,6,ASSERTED,CLEAR). Breaker tripped cycles 1 and 4 (cycle 5 closed at exactly 38). Ground tally: 76. Balance: 20 starting plus 94 fed is 114; 38 on the chain plus 76 to ground is 114. Stage 2 at 10 over its 8 rating is cycle-5 diode return; report it as read.

run.rulesInOwnWords:
Setup: six stages (1 = source, 6 = load). Ratings 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper thresholds 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower thresholds 3,2,4,2,3,2; starting charge 3,6,6,2,2,1; every stage starts CLEAR; the ground tally starts at 0; the breaker setting is 38. Each cycle runs five moves in order, and each move finishes across the whole chain before the next one starts.
1) Charge in: add that cycle's feed to each stage. Ratings are not checked at this point.
2) Shunts: go through stages 1 to 6 in order. If a stage is over its rating, set it to exactly its rating and add the excess to the next stage (i+1). Stage 6's excess goes to ground. Because you walk in order, excess passed down is included when the next stage is checked.
3) Comparators: using the post-shunt charge, a CLEAR stage turns ASSERTED if charge >= its upper threshold. An ASSERTED stage turns CLEAR if charge <= its lower threshold. Otherwise the state stays as it is. Log every flip.
4) Bleed: take a snapshot of all six charges first, then apply every transfer at once. A CLEAR stage loses floor(charge/4) to ground. An ASSERTED stage sends floor(charge/2) to stage i-1, and stage 1's amount goes to ground. States are the ones just set in move 3. Ratings are not checked, so a stage can end above its rating.
5) Breaker: add up the six charges. If the total is strictly greater than 38, every stage becomes floor(charge/2), the total removed goes to ground, and the cycle is recorded as a reset. At 38 or below, nothing happens.

Open Mirror run on the write-up. Mode: filter mode (the default). Topic: the operating rules of the line. Comparison: the electrical language.

Step 1, the rules in plain words. There are six integer counters in a row, numbered 1 to 6. Each has a cap (10,8,12,6,9,7), a high mark (7,6,9,5,7,5) and a low mark (3,2,4,2,3,2). They start at 3,6,6,2,2,1, each with a flag set to CLEAR. A loss tally starts at 0. Each period runs five steps in order:
(1) Add that period's inflows. Caps are not enforced here.
(2) Walk counters 1 to 6. Any counter above its cap is cut back to the cap, and the excess goes to the next counter (counter 6's excess goes to the loss tally). Because the walk is in order, an excess can carry down the chain in the same pass.
(3) Two-level flag. A CLEAR counter becomes ASSERTED when it is at or above its high mark. An ASSERTED counter becomes CLEAR when it is at or below its low mark. Otherwise the flag stays as it is.
(4) Read all values first, then apply all moves at once. A CLEAR counter loses floor(v/4) to the loss tally. An ASSERTED counter passes floor(v/2) to the counter before it (counter 1 passes its share to the loss tally). Caps are not checked.
(5) If the total is strictly greater than 38, every counter becomes floor(v/2) and the amount removed goes to the loss tally. Otherwise nothing happens.

State per stage: an integer charge and a state, CLEAR or ASSERTED. All stages start CLEAR. Starting charge is 3,6,6,2,2,1. Ground starts at 0. Each cycle runs these steps in order, and each step finishes for the whole chain before the next starts.

1. Charge in: add the cycle's feed to each stage. No cap is applied.

2. Shunts: go through stages 1 to 6 in order. If a stage's charge is above its rating (10,8,12,6,9,7), set it to the rating and add the excess to the next stage. Stage 6's excess goes to ground. The next stage is checked after it has received that excess.

3. Comparators: use the charge after shunts. A CLEAR stage with charge at or above its upper threshold (7,6,9,5,7,5) becomes ASSERTED. An ASSERTED stage with charge at or below its lower threshold (3,2,4,2,3,2) becomes CLEAR. Otherwise the state is kept. Log each flip.

5. Breaker: sum the six charges. If the sum is strictly greater than 38, set each stage to floor(charge/2), add the total removed to ground, and record the cycle. If the sum is 38 or less, do nothing.

Conservation check: starting charge plus all feeds equals final chain total plus ground.

domain.label: the pour line (concrete)
domain.mapping: Six pour forms along a chute, form 1 nearest the hopper, form 6 at the end. Quantity: units of mix in the form. Capacity: the form's volume. Spill-over: overtopping runs down the chute into the next form, handled form by form from 1 to 6; overtop from form 6 goes to the waste pit. The two states: a form is GREEN or HOT (HOT set by the upper mark, back to GREEN only at the lower mark; by rule a HOT form can go back to GREEN). Release step: a GREEN form loses a quarter of its mix to evaporation (waste); a HOT form bleeds back half of its mix up the chute into the previous form, all amounts figured from the forms' contents before any is changed. translation.document:
Six forms down the chute: form 1 under the hopper, form 6 at the end. Everything starts GREEN. A cycle is five steps, always in this order, and each step goes all the way down the line before the next one starts.

1. Charge. Each form takes its load off the sheet below. Nobody trims here; a form can sit over capacity for a moment.
2. Overtop. Walk forms 1 to 6. Whatever's over capacity runs down the chute into the next form before you get to that one, so one heavy form can push the whole line. Form 6 overtops into the waste pit.
3. Marks. A GREEN form at or above its upper mark goes HOT. A HOT form at or below its lower mark goes back to GREEN. Anywhere between, it stays what it was. Log every change.
4. Bleed. Read all six first, then move mix. GREEN loses a quarter, rounded down, to evaporation: waste. HOT bleeds half, rounded down, back up the chute into the form before it; form 1's bleed goes to waste. Nothing trims after this, so a form can carry over capacity into the next charge, or finish the run that way.
5. Washout. Total the line. Over 38, halve every form, rounded down, and what comes off is waste. 38 or under, leave it.

run.rulesInOwnWords:
1. Setup: there are six forms in position order 1 to 6. Each has a capacity, an upper mark and a lower mark. Starting quantities are 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1, and every form starts GREEN. Waste starts at 0.
2. A cycle runs five steps in a fixed order. Each step finishes across all six forms before the next step starts.
3. Charge: add that cycle's charge-sheet amount to each form. There is no capping at this step.
4. Overtop: go through the forms in order, 1 to 6. If a form holds more than its capacity, set it to capacity and pass the excess to the next form before checking that form. This lets an overflow cascade down the line. Form 6's excess goes to waste.
5. Marks: using the quantities after overtop, a GREEN form whose quantity is at or above its upper mark becomes HOT. A HOT form whose quantity is at or below its lower mark becomes GREEN. Otherwise the state does not change. At most one change per form per cycle, and every change is logged.
6. Bleed: take a snapshot of all quantities and the post-marks states, then make every move at once. A GREEN form loses floor(q/4), which goes to waste. A HOT form loses floor(q/2), which goes to the form before it (position i-1); form 1's HOT bleed goes to waste. No capacity trim follows, so a form can stay over capacity.
7. Washout: add up the six quantities. If the total is strictly over 38, set each form to floor(q/2) and send the removed amount, q - floor(q/2), to waste. If the total is 38 or less, change nothing.
8. Conservation: start (20) + all charges (94) = end total + waste.

run.rulesInOwnWords:
Six positions (forms) in a row, 1 to 6, each with a capacity, an upper mark and a lower mark. All start GREEN with start quantities 3,6,6,2,2,1. Each cycle runs five steps in fixed order, each step finished across all six positions before the next begins.
1. Charge: add that cycle's charge-sheet amount to each position. No capping yet.
2. Overtop: go 1 to 6 in order. If a position holds more than its capacity, cut it to capacity and add the excess to the next position before that next position is checked (so overflow can cascade). Excess from position 6 goes to waste.
3. Marks: using the post-overtop quantities, a GREEN position with quantity >= upper mark becomes HOT; a HOT position with quantity <= lower mark becomes GREEN; otherwise no change. Each change is logged (cycle, position, before, after).
4. Bleed: snapshot all six quantities and the current states first, then apply all transfers at once. GREEN: lose floor(q/4) to waste. HOT: lose floor(q/2), which goes to the previous position (i-1); position 1's HOT bleed goes to waste. Incoming bleed does not itself bleed this cycle. No capping afterwards, so quantities may exceed capacity.
5. Washout: sum all six. If the sum is strictly greater than 38, each position becomes floor(q/2) and the removed amount goes to waste. If 38 or less, nothing happens.
Waste tally = pit overflow from position 6 + GREEN evaporation + position 1 HOT bleed + washout removals. Conservation: start + all charges = end line total + waste.

I recorded these as content to check, not as the answer. Step 2, pictures: (A) the write-up's concrete pour line (embedded, not counted against the three); (B) a thermostat with a hysteresis band; (C) a cascade of spillway tanks.

Question: can a form flip twice in one cycle? (C) tanks spilling into the next one downstream. Question: is spill passed on to the next tank re-tested in the same pass?
Step 4, breaks: (A) Real concrete does not flow back uphill, and curing does not reverse, but the write-up has HOT forms bleeding upstream and HOT returning to GREEN. Real practice also brings in time, temperature and setting, none of which are in the rules. If someone relied on the picture rather than the rules, it would contradict stated rules (reversible states, backward flow). Because the rules are explicit, they are applied as written. (B) A thermostat acts continuously, but here the marks are checked only once per cycle, after overtop. (C) Tanks do not send anything back upstream or get halved globally. (B) adds nothing, because the rules already state the hysteresis and the once-per-cycle check. (C) adds nothing, because the cascade order is stated. Adds nothing: 3 of 3. Misleading: 0. Not run: 0.

domain.label: the crucible cascade (metallurgy)
domain.mapping: Six crucibles in a cascade, crucible 1 at the charging end, crucible 6 at the tapping end. Quantity: units of melt. Capacity: the crucible's working volume. Spill-over: overflow runs down a launder into the next crucible, handled one crucible at a time from 1 to 6; overflow from crucible 6 goes to the slag pit. The two states: BASE or SUPERHEATED (enters SUPERHEATED at the upper mark, returns to BASE only at the lower mark; by rule the return happens). Release step: a BASE crucible loses a quarter of its melt to slag; a SUPERHEATED crucible sends half of its melt back up a return launder into the previous crucible, all amounts figured from the crucibles' contents before any is changed. Global reset: an emergency tap that halves every crucible, the removed melt going to slag. Loss tally: total to slag.

run.rulesInOwnWords:
Each cycle runs five moves in this order, and each move is finished for all six crucibles before the next one starts.
1) Charge: add the cycle's charge row to each crucible. Volume is not checked at this point.
2) Overflow: go through crucibles 1 to 6 in order. If a crucible holds more than its working volume, cut it back to the volume and add the excess to the next crucible before checking that one, so overflow can chain down the line. Excess from crucible 6 goes to slag. This walk happens once per cycle.
3) Temperature: using the amounts after overflow, a BASE crucible with melt >= its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED, and a SUPERHEATED crucible with melt <= its lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state stays the same. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, from, to).
4) Bleed: take all six readings first (after overflow). Using the state just set in move 3, a BASE crucible loses floor(melt/4) to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible loses floor(melt/2), which is added to the crucible before it; for crucible 1 it goes to slag. All transfers are applied at once from those readings. Amounts left above volume stay until the next cycle's overflow, and after cycle 5 they stay for good.
5) Emergency tap: add up the line. If the total is strictly greater than 38, every crucible is halved: it keeps floor(melt/2), the rest goes to slag, and the cycle is logged as a reset. A total of exactly 38 does not trigger a tap. The tap does not change states.
Slag tally = overflow off crucible 6 + BASE skims + crucible 1's half when SUPERHEATED + tap removals. Balance: start total + all charges = end total + slag.

domain.mapping: Six stem segments from the root collar (segment 1) to the crown (segment 6). Quantity: units of sap. Capacity: the segment's holding volume. Spill-over: excess sap is pushed up the xylem into the next segment toward the crown, handled segment by segment from 1 to 6; excess from segment 6 is transpired away. The two states: QUIET or SINK-ACTIVE (becomes SINK-ACTIVE at the upper mark, back to QUIET only at the lower mark). Release step: a QUIET segment respires away a quarter of its sap; a SINK-ACTIVE segment sends half of its sap back down the phloem into the previous segment toward the root, all amounts figured from the segments' contents before any is changed. Global reset: a leaf-drop event that halves every segment, the removed sap transpired away. Loss tally: total transpired or respired away.

translation.document:
Six compartments, 1 at the bow through 6 at the stern. Water counts in whole units, never below zero. Every pump starts LAMINAR.

Listed 1 to 6:
Volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Inception marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Desinence marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Water at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Emergency blow threshold, whole hull: 38.

Flooding schedule:
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

Each cycle is five steps, in order, each finished in all six before the next.

1. Flood. Add the cycle's water. Don't stop at the volume; let it overfill.

2. Scuppers. Work bow to stern, 1 through 6. Anything above volume runs aft into the next compartment, leaving this one exactly full. Since 1 goes before 2, one surge can carry down the whole line. Whatever overtops 6 goes overboard.

3. Read the pumps. LAMINAR at or above its inception mark goes CAVITATING. CAVITATING only settles to LAMINAR at or below its desinence mark; in between, it holds. Log every change.

4. Pump. Size every discharge off current readings before touching a valve: LAMINAR moves a quarter, CAVITATING half, rounded down. Then open them all together. LAMINAR water goes overboard. CAVITATING water backflows forward into the next compartment toward the bow; out of 1 it goes overboard. Nobody watches volume here, so a compartment can sit overfull until next cycle's scuppers, and after cycle 5 it stays that way.

5. Blow. Sum all six. Strictly over 38: every compartment halves, rounded down, the difference overboard; note the cycle. At 38 or under, leave it.

Keep one running overboard total from zero: overflow off 6, LAMINAR discharge, backflow out of 1, blown water.

Report. At the end of cycle 5 hand in: end water 1 to 6: 6, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2. End states: 1 to 5 CAVITATING, 6 LAMINAR. State changes (cycle, position, before, after), L for LAMINAR, C for CAVITATING: (1,2,L,C), (1,3,L,C), (1,4,L,C), (1,5,L,C), (2,1,L,C), (2,3,C,L), (2,5,C,L), (2,6,L,C), (3,3,L,C), (3,4,C,L), (4,4,L,C), (4,5,L,C), (5,6,C,L). Blows: cycles 1 and 4. Overboard: 76. Balance: 20 at start plus 94 flooded is 114; 38 aboard plus 76 overboard is 114.

Six chambers: 1 at the head, 6 at the tail. Nutrient mass is whole units; any split rounds down.

Chamber limits, 1 to 6: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7. Pupation marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5. Fallback marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2. Starting mass: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1. Every chamber starts LARVAL.

Five cycles per run. Finish each job along the whole line before the next:

1. Feed. Add the cycle's ration:
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0
No trimming yet.

2. Overflow. Walk from 1 to 6. Anything above a chamber's limit moves into the next chamber, so overflow can cascade down the line. Chamber 6's overflow is discarded.

3. Stage check. A LARVAL chamber at or above its pupation mark goes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber at or below its fallback mark goes back to LARVAL; that's routine, log it and move on. Anything in between holds its stage. Log every change as (cycle, chamber, before, after).

4. Metabolism. Weigh all six first, then act. LARVAL chambers burn off a quarter of their mass. PUPAL chambers reabsorb half back into the chamber ahead (one number lower); chamber 1's half is discarded. No trimming: a chamber can stay over limit until next cycle's overflow, or for good after cycle 5.

5. Moult. Total the line. Above 38, every chamber halves and the shed mass is discarded. At 38 or under, leave it.

Keep one loss tally: tail overflow, burn-off, chamber 1's reabsorbed half, moult sheddings.

Report. After cycle 5, hand in: end mass 1 to 6: 6, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2 (chamber 2 over limit is right). End stages: PUPAL, PUPAL, PUPAL, PUPAL, PUPAL, LARVAL. Stage changes: (1,2,LARVAL,PUPAL), (1,3,LARVAL,PUPAL), (1,4,LARVAL,PUPAL), (1,5,LARVAL,PUPAL), (2,1,LARVAL,PUPAL), (2,3,PUPAL,LARVAL), (2,5,PUPAL,LARVAL), (2,6,LARVAL,PUPAL), (3,3,LARVAL,PUPAL), (3,4,PUPAL,LARVAL), (4,4,LARVAL,PUPAL), (4,5,LARVAL,PUPAL), (5,6,PUPAL,LARVAL). Step 1, plain statement. Six stores in a row, numbered 1 to 6. Each has a capacity (10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7), an upper threshold (7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5), a lower threshold (3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2), a starting count (3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1) and a two-valued flag that starts at STEADY. OVERLOADED: floor(count/2) moves back to the previous store, and store 1's amount leaves the system. A store can end above capacity after this step. domain.label: the retrieval tier stack (RAG architecture)
domain.mapping: Six retrieval buffers in a stack, tier 1 closest to the model, tier 6 furthest. Quantity: chunks held. Capacity: the tier's chunk budget. Spill-over: over-budget chunks are evicted to the next tier out, handled tier by tier from 1 to 6; evictions from tier 6 are dropped. The two states: a tier is COLD or HOT (becomes HOT at the upper mark, back to COLD only at the lower mark). Release step: a COLD tier compacts away a quarter of its chunks (dropped); a HOT tier promotes half of its chunks back into the previous tier, all amounts figured from the tiers' contents before any is changed. Global reset: a context reset that halves every tier, the removed chunks dropped. Loss tally: total dropped.

translation.document:
The stack is six retrieval buffers: tier 1 sits next to the LLM, tier 6 furthest out. Everything you track is chunks held.

Per tier, 1 to 6:
Budget: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
HOT mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
COLD mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Holding at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Context ceiling for the whole stack: 38. Every tier starts COLD.

New chunks landing each cycle (tiers 1 to 6):
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

A cycle is five passes, each finished across the whole stack before the next starts.

1. Load. Add the cycle's new chunks. No trimming yet; a tier can sit over budget here.
2. Evict. Walk tier 1 through 6. Anything over budget moves out to the next tier, so it can push that tier over before you reach it. Overflow from tier 6 is dropped.
3. Flag. A COLD tier at or above its HOT mark goes HOT; a HOT tier at or below its COLD mark goes COLD. Anywhere between the marks, it keeps its flag. Log every flip.
4. Rebalance. Off the post-flag counts, a COLD tier compacts a quarter of its chunks (round down), dropped; a HOT tier promotes half (round down) into the tier one closer to the LLM, and tier 1's promotion is dropped. Work out all six amounts before moving anything. A promotion can leave a tier over budget; that waits for next cycle's evict, and after cycle 5 it just stands.
5. Reset check. If the stack totals more than 38, context reset: every tier halves (round down), removed chunks dropped. Exactly 38 is fine.

Keep one running drop count covering tier-6 evictions, compactions, tier-1 promotions and resets.

domain.mapping: A state vector x with six integer components, index 1 to 6. Quantity: the component value. Capacity: a box constraint c_i. Spill-over: a Gauss-Seidel-style sweep from component 1 to 6 that projects each component onto its box and adds the violation to the next component (not a simultaneous Jacobi projection); the violation of component 6 is added to a slack accumulator. The two states: each component has an active-set flag INACTIVE or ACTIVE with hysteresis (activates at the upper threshold, deactivates only at the lower threshold). Release step: a Jacobi-style simultaneous update computed from the current vector: an INACTIVE component sheds floor(x_i/4) to slack; an ACTIVE component moves floor(x_i/2) to component i-1 (component 1 sends it to slack). Global reset: a penalty step that halves every component (floor) when the 1-norm exceeds the budget, the removed amount going to slack. Loss tally: the slack accumulator.

Welcome to the desk. The state is x, six nonnegative integer components, positions 1 to 6, starting at x0 = (3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1). Box bounds c = (10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7). Activation thresholds u = (7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5); deactivation thresholds d = (3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2). Budget on the 1-norm: 38. Slack s starts at 0, and every component starts INACTIVE.

A run is five cycles. Each cycle is five steps, and each step finishes across the whole vector before the next one starts.

1. Load. Add the cycle's row of b to x. Bounds are not enforced here. Rows, cycles 1 to 5: (0,6,3,5,3,3), (4,2,0,1,1,7), (4,4,3,0,0,6), (7,6,7,1,3,0), (0,6,6,3,3,0).

2. Projection sweep, Gauss-Seidel, 1 through 6. Clip x_i to c_i and push the violation into x_{i+1} before you visit it, so overflow cascades down the vector. Component 6's violation goes to s.

3. Active-set update on the projected x. INACTIVE goes ACTIVE at x_i >= u_i; ACTIVE drops back to INACTIVE at x_i <= d_i. Anywhere in between, the flag holds. Log every flip as (cycle, position, before, after).

4. Jacobi shed. Compute all six amounts from the same x before anything moves. An INACTIVE component sheds floor(x_i/4) to s. An ACTIVE component moves floor(x_i/2) up to x_{i-1}; component 1 sends its share to s. No projection after this step: a component can sit over its bound until the next sweep, and after cycle 5 it simply stays there.

domain.mapping: Six teams in a delivery pipeline, team 1 at intake, team 6 at the customer end. Quantity: open tickets. Capacity: the team's WIP limit. Spill-over: tickets over the limit are handed to the next team downstream, handled team by team from 1 to 6; overflow from team 6 is closed-without-action. The two states: a team is ROUTINE or ESCALATED (becomes ESCALATED at the upper mark, back to ROUTINE only at the lower mark). Release step: a ROUTINE team closes a quarter of its tickets; an ESCALATED team bounces half of its tickets back to the previous team, all amounts figured from the teams' counts before any is changed. Global reset: a quarterly backlog purge that halves every team when the total open count exceeds the target, the removed tickets closed-without-action. Loss tally: total closed (by any route). The target is just a number; the document must not add any gaming, incentive, or behavioural rule.

run.rulesInOwnWords:
Setup: six teams in a line, team 1 (intake) to team 6 (customer). Per team: WIP limit 10,8,12,6,9,7; escalate mark 7,6,9,5,7,5; stand-down mark 3,2,4,2,3,2; opening tickets 3,6,6,2,2,1 (20 total). All start ROUTINE. Board target 38. Closed tally starts at 0. Each cycle runs five steps, and each step finishes for all teams before the next starts.
Step 1 (arrivals): add that cycle's new tickets to each team. Limits are not applied here.
Step 2 (walk): go team 1 to team 6 in order. If a team is over its WIP limit, cut it to the limit and pass the excess to the next team. That excess counts toward the next team's total when the walk reaches it, so overflow can cascade. Excess from team 6 is closed-without-action and goes on the closed tally.
Step 3 (status): ROUTINE with tickets >= escalate mark becomes ESCALATED. ESCALATED with tickets <= stand-down mark becomes ROUTINE. Otherwise status stays the same. Each flip is logged with cycle, team, before and after.
Step 4 (work): take one snapshot of all counts after step 2 and use the statuses from step 3. ROUTINE teams close floor(snapshot/4), which goes on the tally. ESCALATED teams send floor(snapshot/2) to the team upstream (team i-1). Team 1's bounce is closed and goes on the tally. Bounced tickets may leave a team over its limit. That is allowed, and they are not re-walked until the next cycle's step 2, or ever after cycle 5.
Step 5 (backlog cut): add up the board. If the total is strictly greater than 38, each team keeps floor(count/2) and the rest are closed-without-action (tally). If the total is 38 or less, nothing happens. A cycle where this fires counts as a reset.
Balance: 20 start + all arrivals = open at end + closed tally.
